Ben / team — initial sizing draft below (high level, conservative numbers to start; happy to iterate after the Wed call).

Workload assumptions (verified from spreadsheet):
- Interactive short prompts: steady 120 qps, avg 60 tokens; expected daily diurnal with campaign spikes to 600 qps for up to 15 minutes.
- Batch embeddings: 200 reqs/min nightly, latency not critical.
- Session affinity expected (KV cache hits ~40% for repeat users).

Sizing suggestions (three-phase plan):
1) Pilot (4 weeks):
   - APAC pilot pool: 8 nodes (A100-40GB equivalent) in Singapore; configured to allow 50 concurrent streams/node with continuous batching and KV cache warmup.
   - EU fallback: 2 standby nodes in Frankfurt to accept overflow asynchronously (higher token latency acceptable).
2) Ramp (1-3 months):
   - APAC production pool: scale to 22 nodes (mix: 18 A100-style for low-latency, 4 cost-tier nodes for embeddings/batch).
   - Configure autoscale policy to add burst buffer of up to +40% using dedicated reserved burst capacity in nearby EU zone before routing to on-demand US nodes.
3) Steady (post 3 months):
   - Target: 30 nodes APAC with sustained autoscale headroom for seasonal peaks.

Performance / config notes:
- Quantization: recommend starting with 8-bit quant (FP16->8-bit) on prod for predictable quality; test 4-bit in parallel on pilot nodes for cost analysis. Flag: certain sampling behaviors differ at 4-bit—require eval set.
- KV / prefix caching: enable prefix caching for sessions to reduce token compute by ~20% on steady flows.
- Latency tradeoffs: hitting <120ms token latency requires A100-equivalent GPUs with optimized kernels and tight batching. T4-class nodes will struggle on interactive latency at scale.
- Operational guardrails: set routing policy with progressive fallback (APAC -> EU reserved -> US reserved -> on-demand cloud) and a circuit-breaker on sustained >60s median token time.

Timeline & SOW ask:
- We can deliver pilot in 2 weeks after SOW and infra permissions; ramp plan requires 4-8 weeks depending on node procurement.

Attachments: draft_sizing_model.csv (node-by-node simulation, conservative/aggressive tabs).

I can convert the above into an SOW line-item breakdown; Ben/Marissa tell me what level of cost detail procurement needs.
